old: and as soon as the Sabbath came he went
new: and right away, on the Sabbath, he went
why: Charter: euthys is "right away", every time, never varied (overrides the pilot's own slips in Mark 1). 1:21 kai euthys tois sabbasin (KJV "straightway on the sabbath day").

old: Just then a man with an unclean spirit
new: And right away a man with an unclean spirit
why: Charter: euthys is "right away", every time, never varied (overrides the pilot's own slips in Mark 1). 1:23 kai euthys ēn (critical text; KJV omits).

old: As soon as they left the synagogue, they went
new: Right away they left the synagogue and went
why: Charter: euthys is "right away", every time, never varied (overrides the pilot's own slips in Mark 1). 1:29 kai euthys ... exelthontes (KJV "forthwith").

old: sent him off at once with a stern warning
new: sent him off right away with a stern warning
why: Charter: euthys is "right away", every time, never varied (overrides the pilot's own slips in Mark 1). 1:43 euthys exebalen (KJV "forthwith sent him away"). Reviewer's "drove him off" not taken: in English it reads as chasing him away.

old: the Pharisees went straight out and started plotting
new: the Pharisees went out and right away started plotting
why: Charter: euthys is "right away", every time, never varied (overrides the pilot's own slips in Mark 1). 3:6 exelthontes ... euthys meta tōn Hērōdianōn (KJV "straightway"); euthys goes with the plotting.

old: they went out to take charge of him
new: they went out to seize him
why: 3:21 kratēsai, "seize, lay hold on" (KJV); the arrest verb of 12:12 and 14:46. "Take charge of" makes the family managerial, not forcible.

old: spoke to them in comparisons
new: spoke to them in parables
why: parabolē is "parables" in 4:2-34 and 12:1, 12:12; one word, one rendering.

old: he is guilty of a lasting sin
new: he is guilty of an eternal sin
why: 3:29 aiōniou hamartēmatos; aiōnios is "eternal" elsewhere in this edition (10:17, 10:30). "Lasting" softens the hardest word in the saying.

old: — or they might turn back, and be forgiven.
new: — so that they won't turn back and be forgiven.
why: 4:12 mēpote epistrepsōsin is purposive, "lest they turn" (KJV "lest at any time they should be converted"); "or they might" reads as mere possibility and blunts the saying.

old: and as soon as pressure or persecution comes because of the word, they fall away right away.
new: and then, when pressure or persecution comes because of the word, right away they fall away.
why: 4:17 eita genomenēs thlipseōs ... euthys skandalizontai: eita is "then"; "as soon as ... right away" doubles the euthys and jingles aloud.

old: And as soon as the crop is ready, he puts in the sickle
new: And when the crop is ready, right away he puts in the sickle
why: Charter: euthys is "right away", every time, never varied (overrides the pilot's own slips in Mark 1). 4:29 hotan de paradoi ho karpos, euthys apostellei to drepanon. Found in the sweep; not in the report.

old: As soon as he stepped out of the boat, a man
new: As he stepped out of the boat, right away a man
why: Charter: euthys is "right away", every time, never varied (overrides the pilot's own slips in Mark 1). 5:2 euthys hypēntēsen autō (KJV "immediately there met him").

old: Swear to God you won't torture me!
new: In God's name, don't torture me!
why: 5:7 horkizō se ton theon (KJV "I adjure thee by God"): the spirit puts Jesus under oath. "Swear to God" is now a casual exclamation. Reviewer's added "I beg you" is not in the Greek and is dropped.

old: She hurried straight back in to the king
new: Right away she hurried back in to the king
why: Charter: euthys is "right away", every time, never varied (overrides the pilot's own slips in Mark 1). 6:25 eiselthousa euthys meta spoudēs (KJV "straightway with haste").

old: and he was moved to the depths for them
new: and his heart went out to them
why: 6:34 splanchnisthē (KJV "moved with compassion"). See Policies: outside the 1:41 crux the plain idiom wins; "heart" keeps the inward-organ image.

old: spend two hundred days' wages on bread
new: spend two hundred denarii on bread
why: 6:37 dēnariōn diakosiōn (KJV "two hundred pennyworth"). Charter keeps biblical coins; 14:5 already has "three hundred denarii".

old: looked up to the sky, gave thanks, broke the loaves, and
new: looked up to the sky, blessed and broke the loaves, and
why: 6:41 eulogēsen, "blessed" (KJV); the edition keeps eulogeō/eucharisteō apart at 8:6-7 and 14:22-23.

old: And somewhere around three in the morning he came
new: And somewhere around the fourth watch of the night he came
why: 6:48 peri tetartēn phylakēn tēs nyktos (KJV "about the fourth watch of the night"). Charter keeps biblical hours.

old: As soon as they got out of the boat, people recognized him.
new: When they got out of the boat, people recognized him right away.
why: Charter: euthys is "right away", every time, never varied (overrides the pilot's own slips in Mark 1). 6:54 euthys epignontes auton (KJV "straightway they knew him").

old: Isaiah was right about you hypocrites.
new: Isaiah prophesied rightly about you hypocrites.
why: 7:6 kalōs eprophēteusen Ēsaias (KJV "Well hath Esaias prophesied"); "was right" drops the verb.

old: asked him about the comparison.
new: asked him about the parable.
why: 7:17 parabolē; "parables" in chapter 4 and 12:1, 12:12. One word, one rendering.

old: I'm moved to the depths for these people.
new: My heart goes out to these people.
why: 8:2 splanchnizomai epi ton ochlon (KJV "I have compassion on the multitude"). Jesus' saying must pass the read-aloud test (charter); see Policies.

old: Peter took him aside and started correcting him.
new: Peter took him aside and started rebuking him.
why: 8:32 epitiman, the same verb as Jesus' "rebuked Peter" in 8:33; "correcting" softens Peter and breaks the echo.

old: he has to say no to himself, and pick up his cross
new: he has to deny himself, and pick up his cross
why: 8:34 aparnēsasthō heauton (KJV "let him deny himself"). "Say no to himself" reads as willpower advice; the famous line stays recognizable.

old: in this unfaithful and sinful generation
new: in this adulterous and sinful generation
why: 8:38 moichalidi, "adulterous" (KJV), the prophets' marriage image; "unfaithful" explains the metaphor away.

old: and as soon as the spirit saw Jesus it convulsed him
new: and when the spirit saw Jesus, right away it convulsed him
why: Charter: euthys is "right away", every time, never varied (overrides the pilot's own slips in Mark 1). 9:20 idōn auton to pneuma euthys synesparaxen auton (KJV "straightway the spirit tare him").

old: Peter started in on him:
new: Peter began to say to him,
why: 10:28 ērxato legein ho Petros autō (KJV "Peter began to say unto him"); "started in on" means to nag or attack.

old: As soon as you enter it you'll find a colt
new: As you enter it, right away you'll find a colt
why: Charter: euthys is "right away", every time, never varied (overrides the pilot's own slips in Mark 1). 11:2 euthys eisporeuomenoi eis autēn heurēsete (KJV "as soon as ye be entered"); pairs with the euthys of 11:3 already rendered "right away".

old: put in two lepta — the smallest coins there are.
new: put in two lepta, which make a quadrans.
why: 12:42 lepta duo, ho estin kodrantēs (KJV "two mites, which make a farthing"). Mark's own aside is restored in place of the editor's gloss; charter keeps biblical coins.

old: Some of them were furious with each other about it:
new: Some of them were indignant, and said to each other:
why: 14:4 aganaktountes pros heautous (KJV "had indignation within themselves"): angry at the waste, speaking among themselves, not angry at each other.

old: As soon as he arrived he went straight up to Jesus
new: When he arrived, right away he went up to Jesus
why: Charter: euthys is "right away", every time, never varied (overrides the pilot's own slips in Mark 1). 14:45 elthōn euthys proselthōn autō (KJV "straightway").

old: And right then a rooster crowed
new: And right away a rooster crowed
why: Charter: euthys is "right away", every time, never varied (overrides the pilot's own slips in Mark 1). 14:72 kai euthys ek deuterou alektōr ephōnēsen (critical text; KJV omits euthys).

old: the chief priests held a council with the elders and the scribes and the whole Sanhedrin.
new: the chief priests made their plans with the elders and the scribes and the whole council.
why: 15:1 symboulion poiēsantes ... holon to synedrion; synedrion is "the council" at 14:55 and 15:43. "Held a council" changed to "made their plans" (symboulion, as at 3:6) to avoid council ... council.

old: It was nine in the morning when they crucified him.
new: It was the third hour when they crucified him.
why: 15:25 ēn de hōra tritē (KJV "the third hour"). The charter names exactly this phrase as one to keep.

old: When noon came, darkness fell over the whole land until three in the afternoon. And at three Jesus
new: When the sixth hour came, darkness fell over the whole land until the ninth hour. And at the ninth hour Jesus
why: 15:33-34 hōras hektēs ... heōs hōras enatēs ... tē enatē hōra (KJV "sixth ... ninth ... ninth hour"). Charter keeps biblical hours.
